ogTitle: Sukhothai 3 Days 2 Nights — Old City, Si Satchanalai & Nature
ogDesc: A full 3-day Sukhothai trip covering UNESCO heritage ruins, the peaceful old town, and misty Khao Luang — with a timed schedule, real costs, and local restaurant tips.
intro: Two days in Sukhothai is doable, but give it 3 days and 2 nights and you'll hit all three sides of the city: the UNESCO old town you can cycle all day, the quieter and lesser-visited Si Satchanalai to the north, and Khao Luang in Ramkhamhaeng National Park for anyone who wants nature. This itinerary flows day by day without backtracking — timed schedule, actual entry fees, and the spots locals eat at.

blocks.html: Quick orientation before we start: Sukhothai splits into two zones that confuse a lot of visitors. New City (Mueang district) is where the hotels, restaurants, and market are. Old City is where the historical park sits, about 12 km away. Si Satchanalai is another 50 km north, and Khao Luang (Ramkhamhaeng National Park) is about 30 km south of town. This itinerary spreads each destination across a separate day so you're not doubling back.

This trip works best if you have your own wheels or rent a car/motorbike in New City — Si Satchanalai and Khao Luang are awkward by public transport. Inside the Old City, a bicycle is by far the best way to get around. No private vehicle? Hiring a day-trip driver to Si Satchanalai and Khao Luang separately makes more sense than piecing together songthaews.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old City: Cycling the UNESCO Heritage Site

blocks.html: Day one belongs entirely to Sukhothai Historical Park. This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the best way to see it is to rent a bicycle and ride — the grounds are wide, shaded in places, and the paths are flat enough that you can pedal at a relaxed pace all day.

items.activity: Leave your hotel in New City and head to Old City (~12 km)
items.note: About 20 min by car. Or catch the shared songthaew from New City to Old City for around THB 20, running every ~30 min.

items.activity: Rent a bicycle near the park entrance + buy zone tickets
items.note: Bike rental THB 20–50/day · Thai visitors: THB 20/zone (THB 40 total for two zones) · Foreigners: THB 100 for the central zone · Bringing a bike in costs an extra THB 10

items.activity: Wat Mahathat — the park's centrepiece, lotus-bud chedis and rows of Buddha images
items.note: This is the royal temple at the heart of the old city — the image most people picture when they think of Sukhothai.

items.activity: Wat Si Sawai + Wat Trapang Ngoen — nearby in the same zone
items.note: Both are a short ride away and share the same ticket zone, so no need to leave.

items.activity: Wat Sa Si — a chedi rising from a lake, stunning reflection in the water
items.note: Morning light keeps the water calm. Get here before midday for the best reflections.

items.activity: Lunch break — Sukhothai noodles near the Old City
items.note: Several shops around the park serve Sukhothai-style noodles (dry style with yard-long beans and red pork). Worth trying here rather than in New City.

items.activity: Ride to the North Zone — Wat Si Chum, home to the massive Phra Achana Buddha in a narrow mondop
items.note: The giant Buddha framed inside the tight stone window is not something you can skip. Wat Si Chum sits just outside the main park boundary in the North Zone.

items.activity: Ramkhamhaeng National Museum
items.note: See replica stone inscriptions and ancient artefacts. Closes around 16:00 — aim to arrive before 15:30.

items.activity: Back into the park for golden hour — shoot Wat Mahathat backlit by the setting sun
items.note: Sunset is when the Old City looks best. The light softens, it cools down, and the crowds thin out.

items.activity: Return to New City for dinner
items.note: Restaurants and the night market are all on the New City side.

blocks.title: Day 1 tip
blocks.html: The historical park is divided into zones (Central, North, West), each with a separate ticket. If you plan to visit all three, buy a combined ticket upfront — it works out cheaper than buying one zone at a time. Bring water and a hat; midday sun can be intense and shade isn't everywhere.

blocks.html: Sukhothai noodles are the dish the city is known for above anything else: thin rice noodles in a lightly sweet clear broth, topped with diagonally-sliced yard-long beans, roasted peanuts, and red pork. These are real spots that are actually open and that locals go to — fit them in between sights depending on which side of town you're on.

items.name: Jae Hae Sukhothai Noodles
items.blurb: Old-recipe Sukhothai noodles with diagonally cut yard-long beans done the traditional way. Open-air wooden shop with a breeze running through it. This is the place that comes up whenever anyone debates where to get the real thing.

items.name: Sukhothai Noodles Ta Pui
items.blurb: A Sukhothai institution that has been around for over 70 years. Order the dry-style Sukhothai noodles — heavy on the toppings, rounded flavour that older generations grew up on.

items.name: Sukhothai Noodles Mai Klang Krung
items.blurb: Another consistently popular Sukhothai noodle shop. The house recipe loads up the toppings and gives you good value. Good stop before heading into the Old City in the morning.

items.name: Baan Khru Iew
items.blurb: Shaded Thai restaurant with old-house atmosphere. The menu covers Sukhothai noodles, pad Thai, khanom buang (crispy pancakes), and desserts — a good sit-down meal rather than a quick bowl.

items.name: Phum Phor
items.blurb: Spacious local-style restaurant with seating in several areas. Serves Thai food and desserts — try the tom yum Sukhothai noodles and fresh coconut ice cream.

blocks.html: Day two takes you further north, about 50 km, to Si Satchanalai Historical Park. It gets far fewer visitors than the Sukhothai Old City and the forest and hills surrounding the ruins make it feel completely different. If you want peace and the rawer atmosphere of an ancient city, this is it.

items.activity: Leave New City and drive north to Si Satchanalai (~50 km)
items.note: About 1 hour by car. No private vehicle? A hired day-trip driver is much easier than public buses for this route.

items.activity: Arrive at the park — buy tickets + rent a bike or board the tram
items.note: Thai visitors THB 10 · Foreigners THB 30 · Bike rental THB 20–30 · Tram THB 30/loop with a guide commentary

items.activity: Wat Chang Lom — Sri Lankan-style chedi ringed by stucco elephants at the base
items.note: This is Si Satchanalai's headline sight. The elephant row around the base is remarkably intact.

items.activity: Wat Chedi Jet Thaew — a row of chedis in different forms side by side
items.note: The stucco work and arched niches still show fine detail up close. Worth walking slowly.

items.activity: Wat Nang Phaya — intricate floral stucco panels on the viharn walls
items.note: The floral stucco patterns on the outer wall are among the most detailed and rare examples of the period.

items.activity: Lunch in Si Satchanalai town
items.note: Made-to-order shops and noodle stalls in the district centre — no need to drive back to Sukhothai.

items.activity: Sangkhalok Kiln Preservation Centre (Tao Thuriang)
items.note: See the actual excavated ancient kilns that produced Sangkhalok ceramics and learn how they were once exported across the region.

items.activity: Pick up Sangkhalok ceramics as souvenirs
items.note: Fish and floral motifs are the signature patterns of Sukhothai Sangkhalok ware. Small pieces are easy to pack.

items.activity: Drive back to New City
items.note: Arrive by evening — rest up and find dinner in town.

blocks.title: Day 2 tip
blocks.html: Si Satchanalai has more tree cover than Sukhothai Old City but some paths are loose sand — if you're cycling, pick a bike with slightly wider tyres. Alternatively, one tram loop covers the main temples if you'd rather not pedal.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Khao Luang, Ramkhamhaeng National Park

blocks.html: The final day switches from ancient ruins to forest. Ramkhamhaeng National Park (Khao Luang) is about 30 km south of town. Khao Luang peak sits at 1,200 m — the highest point in the province. The summit trail is 3.7 km and takes 3–4 hours; it's a solid hike for anyone who's up for it. If you're not keen on the full climb, the nature trail near the park headquarters through forest and along streams is worthwhile on its own.

items.activity: Check out + drive to Ramkhamhaeng National Park (~30 km)
items.note: Park open 08:00–16:30 daily · Entry: adults THB 40, children THB 20

items.activity: Arrive at park HQ and register
items.note: If you want to camp on the summit, book in advance and confirm conditions with the park — they'll have details on what's open.

items.activity: Nature trail around park HQ / summit hike up Khao Luang (for the fit)
items.note: Summit trail: 3.7 km, 3–4 hrs, steady elevation gain. Casual option: short loop through forest and along the stream near HQ.

items.activity: Lunch from packed food or snacks you've brought
items.note: Food options inside the park are limited. Bring water and enough food for the day.

items.activity: Descend and take in the green forest on the way back
items.note: Late rainy season through early cool season (Oct–Dec) is when the forest is at its greenest and mist clings to the slopes — the most popular time to hike Khao Luang.

items.activity: Leave the park and continue your journey
items.note: Leave enough time to clear the park before 16:30 closing, and before dark — some sections of the mountain road have no lighting.

blocks.title: Before you hike Khao Luang
blocks.html: The summit hike takes real effort and the weather changes fast at altitude. Check with the park whether the summit trail is open for your dates — some sections close during heavy rainy season. If you're travelling with young children or elderly family members, the short nature trail near park HQ is the safer and still rewarding option.

blocks.text: Rough Budget per Person (accommodation not included)

items: Sukhothai Historical Park entry — Thai visitors: combined THB 40 + bike entry THB 10 (Foreigners: THB 100 for central zone)
Si Satchanalai — entry THB 10 (Thai) + bike THB 20–30 or tram THB 30
Food — noodle bowl THB 40–65 · sit-down meal THB 150–300/person
Getting around — songthaew New City→Old City around THB 20/trip · hired vehicle for Si Satchanalai/Khao Luang: ask for price in advance

blocks.html: The most comfortable window is November through February: mild temperatures, manageable sun, and the forests around Khao Luang are still lush coming out of rainy season. If your dates line up with the Loy Krathong festival (mid-November), Sukhothai puts on the biggest celebration in the country — the ruins are lit up and it's genuinely atmospheric. The downside: prices spike, accommodation sells out weeks in advance, and the Old City gets very crowded. Book early if you're aiming for festival dates. In hot season (March–May), start early each day and take a proper midday break — cycling in the afternoon sun is rough.

faq.q: Is 3 days and 2 nights enough for Sukhothai?
faq.a: Yes, and it's a good fit. Day one covers the Sukhothai Historical Park by bike, day two takes you to Si Satchanalai and the Sangkhalok kilns, and day three closes out with nature at Khao Luang. You get the history and the nature without feeling rushed.

faq.q: Can I visit Sukhothai without a private vehicle?
faq.a: For the Old City, yes easily — catch the shared songthaew from New City (around THB 20) and rent a bicycle inside. But Si Satchanalai and Khao Luang are far out and public transport is inconvenient. For those days, hire a driver for the day or rent a motorbike/car from New City.

faq.q: How much does it cost to enter Sukhothai Historical Park?
faq.a: Thai visitors pay THB 20 per zone, or a combined ticket for THB 40. Foreigners pay around THB 100 for the central zone. Bringing a bicycle in costs an extra THB 10. Students, monks, and visitors aged 60 and over enter free.

faq.q: What's the difference between Sukhothai Old City and Si Satchanalai?
faq.a: Sukhothai Old City is the main UNESCO site right outside town — well-maintained, popular with visitors, and easy to cycle. Si Satchanalai is 50 km further north, quieter, surrounded by hills and forest, and gets far fewer tourists. Go there if you want the ruins to yourself and a more rugged atmosphere.

faq.q: Do I have to hike to the summit at Khao Luang?
faq.a: Not at all. The full summit trail is 3.7 km and takes 3–4 hours — good for those who want the workout and the views. If you're with family or would rather take it easy, the shorter nature trail near park headquarters through forest and alongside streams is still worth the visit.
